description: Presentations on Biohacking at DEF CON 23 covers medical device security, honeypot deployment for healthcare infrastructure, and the ethical frontiers of human augmentation.

talks.title: Medical Devices: Pwnage and Honeypots
talks.teaser: Scott Erven and Mark Collao demonstrate systemic security failures across connected medical devices and reveal findings from deploying specialized healthcare honeypots.
talks.summary:
The Insecure Landscape of Healthcare IT

Scott Erven details an extensive multi-year investigation into the cybersecurity posture of medical equipment across healthcare facilities. Critical clinical systems—including drug infusion pumps, anesthesia workstations, patient monitors, and radiology networks—regularly operate with minimal security controls directly connected to hospital local area networks.

Pervasive Hardcoded Credentials and Unpatched Systems

Erven reveals systemic vulnerabilities across major medical device manufacturers, including hardcoded administrative credentials, unencrypted proprietary protocols, and unpatched legacy operating systems. Attackers on hospital networks can alter dosage limits on infusion pumps, manipulate telemetry readings on intensive care monitors, or induce denial-of-service conditions on life-critical equipment.

Deploying Clinical Honeypots

To understand threat actor interest in healthcare targets, Erven and his team deployed customized medical device honeypots simulating operational hospital infrastructure. The honeypots attracted automated botnet intrusions, unauthorized remote access attempts via exposed management interfaces, and sophisticated reconnaissance targeting healthcare delivery networks.

Strategic Recommendations for Clinical Cyber Defense

Mitigating medical device risk requires coordinated action across hospital procurement, clinical engineering, and device manufacturers. Erven advocates for strict network segmentation of clinical equipment, rigorous pre-procurement security evaluations, rapid vulnerability disclosure frameworks, and removing administrative backdoors from healthcare technology.
